scope: literal-environment learning diagnostic; corridor containment unresolved
reconstruction_choices: This is a literal-environment learning diagnostic with unresolved corridor containment. Development evaluation is used for selection, is not held-out evidence, and does not authorize delay experiments.

One native environment is reset for fresh training seeds training_scenario_seed_start + completed_episodes. No pre-birth transitions are fabricated. All sampled aircraft trajectories end at arrival or declared deadline failure with zero bootstrap before one PPO update.

Initialization, Python and NumPy use training_seed; training action sampling and PPO shuffling use separate saved CPU torch.Generator streams. Evaluation samples use dev_action_seed_base + case seed, reset identically for each policy checkpoint.

The complete 12-case development set is declared before learning, cycling 3/4/5 corridors. No Resolution and sampled policy share each exact generated scenario. NR is cached once per geometry per job. Optional argmax is reported separately and never selects the checkpoint.

Aggregate rates divide summed unordered pair-seconds by summed flight-hours, retaining failed-flight exposure. Among models with completed/planned >=0.95, lower NMAC seconds per flight-hour wins, then lower LoWC. Before eligibility, higher completed fraction wins, then NMAC and LoWC. Exact ties keep the earlier checkpoint.

Run initial evaluation before updating, periodic evaluation every 50 completed episodes and final evaluation of the latest model when time allows. Evaluation cases restricted by --eval-limit are explicitly marked a smaller development diagnostic and form part of checkpoint compatibility.

--episodes is the target total number of completed training episodes, including any resumed episodes. --wall-seconds is an inner wall-clock budget beginning at CLI entry; the outer launcher must allow additional import/startup/exit time.

Before starting another training episode, reserve measured evaluation time and a save grace period. Check the inner cutoff at each environment decision. An interrupted episode is discarded, its pre-episode RNG states restored, and its scenario seed remains next; it is not updated or reported completed.

Atomic latest.pt is written initially, every 10 completed episodes and on orderly exit; best.pt follows the predeclared development selection. latest.pt embeds the selected best checkpoint so a resumed isolated job does not need an undeclared sibling file. Checkpoints contain only weights-only-loadable tensors/primitives, optimizer state, exact configs, versions, counters and RNG states.
